(فَأَلْقى عَصاهُ فَإِذا هِيَ ثُعْبانٌ مُبِينٌ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; ألقى is a past verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "he"; عصاه is the direct object. In فإذا the fāʾ is a conjunction and إذا is the "suddenness" إذا, which is an adverbial or a particle, and its discussion has already been given in detail; هي is the mubtadaʾ, ثعبان the khabar and مبين an adjective. The "wasp question" and the dispute of Sībawayh with al-Kisāʾī over it in the presence of Yaḥyā al-Barmakī has already been discussed. (وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُ فَإِذا هِيَ بَيْضاءُ لِلنَّاظِرِينَ) This sentence is conjoined to the one before it, and is like it in its parsing.
(قالَ لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُ إِنَّ هذا لَساحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ) قال فرعون; للملأ is attached to قال; حوله is an adverbial attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl. Al-Zamakhsharī has an ingenious treatment of its parsing, which we cite for its splendour:
"If you say: What governs حوله? I say: It is accusative in two ways, an accusative in form and an accusative in position. The governor of the formal accusative is what is implied in the adverbial, and the governor of the positional accusative is the accusative as ḥāl."
إن is a particle resembling the verb, and هذا is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām; ساحر is the khabar and عليم a second khabar. (يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُخْرِجَكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِكُمْ بِسِحْرِهِ) The clause is an adjective of ساحر. It is a complete line of the majzūʾ al-rajaz metre, yet is not poetry, because intention is absent, and this has been discussed in detail before. أن and what is within its scope is the object of يريد; من أرضكم is attached to يخرجكم, and بسحره is also attached to يخرجكم.
(فَماذا تَأْمُرُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; ماذا is an interrogative noun, the direct object of تأمرون, or an absolute object because it is in the sense of a maṣdar; or ما is an interrogative noun and ذا a relative noun, the khabar, and the clause تأمرون the ṣila. He said that after what he had seen dazzled him and bewilderment and amazement overcame him. (قالُوا أَرْجِهْ وَأَخاهُ وَابْعَثْ فِي الْمَدائِنِ حاشِرِينَ) قالوا is a verb and agent; أرجه is an imperative verb and the hāʾ is the direct object; أخاه is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment) or is conjoined to the hāʾ; وابعث is conjoined to أرجه; في المدائن is attached to ابعث; and حاشرين is an adjective of an omitted direct object, that is, "police (shuraṭ) who will gather the magicians and bring them together". (يَأْتُوكَ بِكُلِّ سَحَّارٍ عَلِيمٍ) يأتوك is an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the answer to the imperative; بكل سحار is attached to يأتوك; and عليم is an adjective of سحار.

* Benefits:
Al-shurṭ: its singular is shurṭī. They are a group of the best of the helpers of rulers, and in our days they are the chiefs of the police and its men. They were so named because they made for themselves a mark by which they were known. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "Al-sharaṭ, with vowels on the letters, are the guards; they were so named because they made for themselves a mark by which they were known." Al-shurṭa is also the first battalion to take part in battle and to prepare for death.

dervis-irab:38-44.t:
* I'rab:
(فَجُمِعَ السَّحَرَةُ لِمِيقاتِ يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ) The fāʾ is a conjunction upon an implied element; جمع is a passive past verb and السحرة the deputy agent; لميقات is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جمع; يوم is a muḍāf ilayhi and معلوم an adjective. The "known day" is the day of adornment (yawm al-zīna), and its appointed time is the forenoon (waqt al-ḍuḥā); its mention has already passed in [Sūrat] Ṭāhā, so he renewed the reference with it. (وَقِيلَ لِلنَّاسِ: هَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُجْتَمِعُونَ؟) وقيل is conjoined to what precedes; للناس is attached to it; هل is a particle of interrogation; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ and مجتمعون its khabar; the clause is the content of the saying. In the interrogation there is the sense of a command, as though he were finding them slow and urging them to gather. Among this is the saying of Taʾabbaṭa Sharran:
هل أنت باعث دينار لحاجتنا ... أو عبد رب أخا عوف بن مخراق
(Gloss: Will you send Dīnār for our need, or ʿAbd Rabb, the brother of ʿAwf ibn Mikhrāq?)
Here هل is an interrogative of impatience (istifhām istibṭāʾī) containing an urging to act. دينار is the name of a man, and رب likewise, and it is accusative because it is conjoined to the position of دينار, since it is an object in meaning; أخا عوف is an adjective of it, and it is said to be a vocative. ʿAwf and Mikhrāq are the names of two men, and it is reported "ʿAwn" with a nūn. (لَعَلَّنا نَتَّبِعُ السَّحَرَةَ إِنْ كانُوا هُمُ الْغالِبِينَ) The clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, because the hope is with regard to the state of victory which requires following, though their original intention was that they should not follow Moses; the meaning is: hoping that victory would be theirs so that Moses would not be followed. لعل with its noun, and the clause نتبع is its khabar; السحرة is the direct object; إن is conditional; كانوا is the protasis, being kāna with its noun; هم is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) and الغالبين the khabar of كانوا. (فَلَمَّا جاءَ السَّحَرَةُ قالُوا لِفِرْعَوْنَ أَإِنَّ لَنا لَأَجْراً إِنْ كُنَّا نَحْنُ الْغالِبِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is temporal, adverbial, or a connective; جاء السحرة is a verb and agent; the clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; لفرعون is attached to قالوا; the hamza is interrogative; إن is a particle resembling the verb; لنا is its fronted khabar and أجرا its postponed noun; إن is conditional; كنا is kāna with its noun and is the protasis; نحن is a separating pronoun and الغالبين the khabar of كنا; and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes, because his words أئن لنا لأجرا are in the sense of the apodosis, as they indicate it. (قالَ نَعَمْ وَإِنَّكُمْ إِذاً لَمِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ) قال فرعون; نعم is a particle of answer, that is, "you shall have the reward"; and he added to them with his words وإنكم, which is a conjunction; إن with its noun; إذن is a particle of answer and requital; the lām is the shifted lām; and من المقربين is the khabar of إن. He promised them the reward and nearness and standing with him. (قالَ لَهُمْ مُوسى أَلْقُوا ما أَنْتُمْ مُلْقُونَ) قال لهم موسى is a verb and agent; لهم is attached to قال; the clause ألقوا is the content of the saying; ما is the direct object; the clause أنتم ملقون is the ṣila; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ and ملقون its khabar. (فَأَلْقَوْا حِبالَهُمْ وَعِصِيَّهُمْ وَقالُوا بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّا لَنَحْنُ الْغالِبُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; ألقوا is a verb and agent; حبالهم is the direct object; عصيهم is conjoined to حبالهم; وقالوا is conjoined to فألقوا. In بعزة the bāʾ is a particle of oath and of genitive, and عزة is genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "we swear and take oath by the might of Pharaoh". إنا is إن with its noun, its hamza being obligatorily kasra because it follows an oath, as has gone before; the lām is the shifted lām; نحن is a separating pronoun or a mubtadaʾ; and الغالبون is the khabar of إنا or the khabar of نحن, the clause being the khabar of إنا.

dervis-irab:45-51.t:
* I'rab:
(فَأَلْقى مُوسى عَصاهُ فَإِذا هِيَ تَلْقَفُ ما يَأْفِكُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; ألقى موسى عصاه is a verb, agent and direct object; in فإذا the fāʾ is a conjunction and إذا is the "suddenness" إذا; هي is a mubtadaʾ and the clause تلقف its khabar; ما is the direct object and the clause يأفكون is the ṣila of ما, that is, "it swallows what they turn away from its true face by their deceptive embellishment, and forge". (فَأُلْقِيَ السَّحَرَةُ ساجِدِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; ألقي is a passive past verb and السحرة the deputy agent. The agent for whom the direct object stood in, had it been stated, is Allah the Mighty and Majestic, through the success He inspired in them, or their faith, or what they witnessed of the dazzling miracle before which the matter of magic shrank. More discussion of "casting" (ilqāʾ) will come in the chapter on rhetoric. ساجدين is a ḥāl [Translator's note: the source prints «ماجدين», evidently a misprint for «ساجدين»]. (قالُوا آمَنَّا بِرَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) The clause آمنا, of verb and agent, is the content of the saying; برب العالمين is attached to آمنا; and the clause of saying is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from ألقي, or a ḥāl with an implied قد. (رَبِّ مُوسى وَهارُونَ) رب is a badal from رب العالمين, or an ʿaṭf bayān; موسى وهارون is a muḍāf ilayhi. (قالَ آمَنْتُمْ لَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ آذَنَ لَكُمْ) The clause آمنتم is the content of the saying; له is attached to آمنتم, and the adverbial likewise; أن and what is within its scope is in the position of genitive by annexation; and لكم is attached to آذن.
(إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ الَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ السِّحْرَ فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ) A justification of their submission to Moses and Aaron, and a deception of his people, lest they believe that the magicians had believed with insight and the appearance of truth. إن with its noun; the shifted lām; كبيركم is the khabar of إن; الذي is an adjective; the clause علمكم is the ṣila; the kāf is a first direct object and السحر a second direct object. In فلسوف the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ, that is, "if you persist in what you did, then you will soon know the evil consequence of what you did"; the lām is the preparatory lām of an oath; سوف is a particle of the future; and تعلمون is an imperfect verb and agent, the object being omitted as we have implied.
(لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِنْ خِلافٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ) The lām is the preparatory lām of an oath; لأقطعن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I"; the clause has no grammatical position because it is explicative, serving as clarification of what he left vague with his words فلسوف تعلمون; أيديكم is the direct object; أرجلكم is conjoined to أيديكم; and من خلاف is a ḥāl, that is, joined together: each one's right hand with his left foot. This has been discussed before. ولأصلبنكم is conjoined to لأقطعن, and أجمعين is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the kāf. (قالُوا: لا ضَيْرَ إِنَّا إِلى رَبِّنا مُنْقَلِبُونَ) لا is the lā of generic negation and its noun is indeclinable on the fatḥa, and its khabar is omitted, that is, "there is no harm upon us and no distress" [Translator's note: the source prints «لا ضمير علينا», evidently a misprint for «لا ضير علينا»; here and in the preceding clause it reads «ضمير اسمها», "its noun, a pronoun"; translated as written]. The clause إنا is a justification for the absence of harm; إن with its noun; إلى ربنا is attached to منقلبون; and منقلبون is the khabar of إنا. (إِنَّا نَطْمَعُ أَنْ يَغْفِرَ لَنا رَبُّنا خَطايانا أَنْ كُنَّا أَوَّلَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) إن with its noun, and the clause نطمع its khabar, the agent being latent, its implied form being "we". أن and what is within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "in the forgiveness of our sins"; or else by incorporating into نطمع the sense of نرجو ("we hope"), so that أن and what is within its scope is in the position of accusative as an object. ربنا is the agent of يغفر and خطايانا the direct object. أن and what is within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "because we were", or the bāʾ, so that the implication is "by reason of our being"; كان with its noun, and أول المؤمنين its khabar, that is, the first of those who believed among Pharaoh's subjects.

* Rhetoric:
In his words «فألقي السحرة ساجدين» there is a metaphor with the vehicle omitted (istiʿāra makniyya), as though they were seized and flung upon their faces. What has added beauty to this metaphor is conformity (mushākala), because he expressed the falling prostrate by "were cast" (ulqiya) and did not say "so they fell down prostrate", in conformity with the earlier castings.
